content: If you are experiencing side effects, it is important to seek medical advice. In Canada, contact your doctor for guidance regarding side effects. Precautions: Before starting pyrimethamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. During pregnancy, pyrimethamine should only be used if absolutely necessary. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Folic acid is particularly important during pregnancy. Be aware that this medication can pass into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and Medical Tests: While taking this medication, regular laboratory tests (such as complete blood counts and liver function tests) should be conducted. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Usage Instructions: Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. To reduce nausea and vomiting, take it with food. If vomiting is severe or persistent, your doctor may adjust your dose or advise you to stop taking the medication. Your doctor will prescribe folic or folinic acid to prevent blood-related complications caused by pyrimethamine. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. This medication works best when its levels in your body are kept constant. Take this drug and any other antiparasitic medications regularly, exactly as prescribed. The dosage is determined based on the type of infection, your medical condition, age, and response to treatment. The duration of treatment depends on the infection being treated. Your doctor will carefully adjust your dose to treat the infection and minimize the risk of serious side effects. Do not take more or less of this medication than prescribed, and do not stop taking it before completing the prescribed course unless directed by your doctor, even if you feel better. Side Effects: Nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Some individuals taking this medication may develop serious side effects, including blood-related complications, particularly at higher doses. This risk can be reduced with the use of folic or folinic acid and regular blood tests. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor. For medical advice about side effects, U.S. residents should contact their doctor, and Canadian residents should do the same.
